thread:
customer-ops: FYI — customer (AcmeCorp) reporting intermittent 503s from their private API. Affects calls to api.internal.acme.svc only from some us-west-2 VPC subnets; a few AZs see NXDOMAIN and then 503s upstream.

mike_s: Can you paste the dig output from the failing node?

customer-ops: here's dig from their app node (us-west-2a):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.internal.acme.svc @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 53821
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.internal.acme.svc. IN A
```

mike_s: thanks. Did they do any hosted zone changes recently (merges / consolidations)?

customer-ops: they merged tenant private zones into a shared private hosted zone "internal.acme.svc" this morning at ~07:10 UTC.

ting: suspicious. Route53 private hosted zones will only resolve in VPCs they're associated with. If one VPC wasn't associated during the merge you'll see NXDOMAIN from that VPC. Also watch for duplicate zones in other accounts.

sara: also check VPC resolver rules and outbound endpoint configs in us-west-2 — a misconfigured forwarder could cause partial success.

mike_s: can someone run dig from a node that egresses via the NAT in the same VPC? That tells us whether it's subnet-scoped.

customer-ops: dig from the NAT (10.0.1.5) returns the expected A record. So NAT subnet resolves, app subnet (10.0.2.x) gets NXDOMAIN.

jordan: that looks like a VPC association issue or a per-VPC resolver rule — the hosted zone might be associated to one VPC but not the other.

mike_s: please run these AWS checks:
`aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z123EXAMPLE`
and
`aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE`

customer-ops: partial outputs: hosted zone Z123EXAMPLE shows vpcCount=1 and lists vpc-0abcde12345. The affected VPC vpc-0fghij67890 is NOT in the association list.

ting: there you go. After the merge the second VPC wasn't associated. That will produce exactly the behavior you describe (some subnets get NXDOMAIN depending on which VPC/resolver they hit).

sara: quick mitigation: add vpc-0fghij67890 to the hosted zone associations. If this is cross-account, use the authorization token flow (the account owning the zone must authorize the association).

mike_s: also consider a forwarding resolver rule if cross-account association is not desirable: create an outbound resolver rule in the calling VPC that forwards `internal.acme.svc` queries to the resolver IPs in the owning account.

customer-ops: ops tried from Console earlier and saw "Authorization required" when associating cross-account. They'll re-run with the auth token.

jordan: note: once association is added, some nodes may still hit NXDOMAIN due to local DNS caches (dnsmasq, nscd). Restart or flush the caches on app hosts.

customer-ops: one more issue they saw before fix — intermittent TLS name mismatch: `curl` showed "SSL: certificate subjectAltName does not match" for api.internal.acme.svc. Could this be related?

ting: possible. If some requests were resolving to an old internal CNAME or an old ALB backend that uses a cert for a different hostname you will see TLS SAN mismatches. That can be caused by split resolution where different nodes get different DNS records during the mis-association window.

mike_s: action items (summary):
1) customer infra to add VPC vpc-0fghij67890 to hosted zone Z123EXAMPLE (complete cross-account authorization if needed)
2) clear DNS cache on app nodes (dnsmasq/nscd/systemd-resolved) after association
3) if TLS mismatch persists, verify internal ALB/NLB certs and CNAMEs / A records to ensure all backends present the correct SANs
4) escalate to eng-sre oncall if still failing after 30m with dig + curl outputs

customer-ops: assigning to customer infra team and re-running association now. Will update here.

oncall: Pinging eng-sre oncall to standby. If you need AWS support, post the dig and curl and I'll open a case.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2246 and assigned to eng-sre-oncall.

customer-ops: Update: association completed at 07:42 UTC, caches cleared, app calls now return 200s and TLS mismatch cleared after backend sync.

mike_s: Great — thanks for the quick triage. Closing the thread. :tada:
